items.title: The universal property of the first order infinitesimal neighbourhood of an immersion
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section on infinitesimal neighbourhoods

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states the universal property of the first order infinitesimal neighbourhood Z' of an immersion i : Z -> X: every commutative diagram with a first order thickening T contained in T' over X admits a unique morphism (a', a) : (T contained in T') -> (Z contained in Z') of thickenings over X, and the analogous statement holds for the n-th order neighbourhood Z_n (statement lines 701-726). The proof converts the universal property into a statement about ideals: after replacing X by the open U in which Z is cut out by I, one shows b^#(b^{-1}I) contained in J, so square-zero-ness of J gives b^#(b^{-1}(I^2)) = 0, and the standard factorisation criterion then produces a' (proof lines 731-741). What makes this non-trivial to guess is that the square-zero hypothesis on the thickening, not merely the diagram, is what makes the factorisation exist at all. The claim is H2; the author proves only part (1) and leaves the higher order statement to the analogous argument, which is reproduced as written.
